clue.text: Drawn gibe, after name released

indicators.note: once the name is released it is let go from the word for a gibe, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a gibe is a taunt, a mocking remark

explanation.surface: A mocking remark, made once someone's name has been let out, sounds like a tense moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn tight, like a stretched rope, is a synonym for tense or tight.

clue.text: Permitted priest to seize house in US state

parts.note: OK means allowed or permitted

indicators.note: the priest is said to seize the house, holding it inside himself

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A priest given permission to take over a home somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state in the south-central United States, an example of the category named.

clue.text: ID etc. apparently carried by person

indicators.note: something carried by a person sits inside them, so the short word goes into the other

parts.note: PERS is a dictionary abbreviation for person
AP is an abbreviation of apparently

explanation.surface: Identity cards and similar items, the sort of thing someone keeps on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of what one carries; 'carried by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity documents are commonly called one's documents, as in an officer asking to see them.

clue.text: The workers' worker, say, a man on the rise in a mine

indicators.note: the man and the article sit inside the word for a mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for a man reads upwards, back to front

parts.note: sir is a polite word for a man

explanation.surface: A worker for the workers, perhaps a man moving up while working in a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker bees are 'the workers', so the person who looks after them is their worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper tends worker bees, so a keeper of hives is cheekily called the worker of the workers.

clue.text: Single income, nothing less? That's very spiritual

indicators.note: less means without, so the zero is taken out of the combined words

parts.note: one means single
O, the zero shape, means nothing
a wage is an income from work

explanation.surface: Living on one income with nothing to spare is called a very spiritual way of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The alternative-spirituality movement of crystals and meditation is described by this label, so it fits 'very spiritual'.

clue.text: Unoriginal option?

definitions.meaning: something copied or borrowed from earlier work is unoriginal
in finance, an option to buy or sell is a contract whose value comes from an underlying asset

explanation.surface: A choice that isn't original, put as a question.
explanation.definitionFit: An unoriginal work copies others; in finance, futures and options are traded contracts of the same name.

clue.text: Pound, deposited in appropriate place, gets nothing

indicators.note: the pound is deposited inside the place, as money is paid in

parts.note: a bank is the appropriate place to deposit money
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Money paid into a bank, yet the account shows nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank is an empty space or zero result, so it can mean nothing at all.

clue.text: Book and article note North American coloured cloth

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A book and an article note a piece of coloured North American fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large spotted or patterned handkerchief, a coloured cloth tied round the head or neck.

clue.text: Thanks returned with gift right now

indicators.note: returned means the word for thanks is turned back to front

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Thanks sent back along with a gift, straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means currently or at this moment, an idiomatic equivalent of right now.

clue.text: Bond getting money invested for a period

indicators.note: money invested is put inside something, so the letter goes into the word for bond

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: A bond with money invested in it for a fixed term.
explanation.definitionFit: A period is a stretch of time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Performance by seed or new version of gamete

indicators.note: a new version of the word is a reworking of its letters

explanation.surface: Something a seed does, or a reworked version of a reproductive cell, as if from biology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed' and 'gamete' paint a plant-biology scene; the seed is a seeded tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: A seeded tennis player performs in a match measured by games, so this tennis phrase is their performance.

clue.text: Latin bird jams bank machine, doing things the old way

indicators.note: the bird jams itself inside the cash machine

parts.note: ATM is a cash machine at a bank
avis is the Latin word for bird

explanation.surface: A bird from Latin gets stuck in a cash machine, an old-fashioned mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavism is reversion to ancestral traits or old habits, a return to earlier ways.

clue.text: A role hardships played for poetic hero

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, rearranged as an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: An actor's role, its hardships played out, makes a hero of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's poem cycle centres on a young countryman of that county, the hero of the poetry.

clue.text: Marine squatter — the crime mostly disturbed and upset lawyers

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, thrown into a new order
mostly means all but the final letter of the word for an offence is used
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: A squatter by the sea, with crime largely upsetting the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims crime to CRIM; THE plus CRIM shuffled ('disturbed') give HERMITC; 'upset' turns BAR into RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean lives in shells abandoned by other creatures, so it squats in someone else's home under the sea.

clue.text: Food item is hot and cold with imitation garnishing

indicators.note: the inner letters garnish the word for imitation, sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: a fake is an imitation
H is short for hot, as on a tap
C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dish that is both hot and cold, decorated with fake trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of fish and potato is a common food item in Britain.

clue.text: Irish vehicle brought in a new backing group

indicators.note: the Irish vehicle is brought into the reversed pair of letters
backing means the pair of letters runs backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An Irish van is brought into a new backing band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like a backing group but turns A and N into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was a famous American grunge rock band, an example of a group.

clue.text: More skilful student dismissed with tirade? That's not normal

indicators.note: the student is dismissed, sent out of the word for more skilful

parts.note: abler means more capable or skilful
L is a learner, the student driver's plate
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A more able student is thrown out after a rant, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant describes behaviour departing from the usual, so it means abnormal or deviant.

clue.text: Capital city — is library in it knocked over?

indicators.note: knocked over means everything is overturned, reading from the end back to the start
the library sits inside the word it

explanation.surface: A question about whether the library in a capital has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the whole string back to front, which the parse's order cannot show at a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Georgia in the Caucasus, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: I leave after I'm getting particular skin disease

indicators.note: the I and the word for leave come after the earlier parts

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe gives the letters
a pet subject is one's particular favourite
go means leave

explanation.surface: Someone saying they will leave once they get a certain skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection of the skin, an example of a skin disease.

clue.text: Idiomatic use of statistic quoted in Parliament?

definitions.meaning: a metaphor or idiom is language used non-literally
a number cited during an address in the Commons is literally a number within a speech

explanation.surface: Using idiom, or quoting a number in a parliamentary debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor or idiom is an expression not meant literally, the standard term for idiomatic usage.

clue.text: Last month having sect dumping leader? It's one month on

indicators.note: dumping the leader means the first letter of the word for sect is dropped

parts.note: a cult is a sect
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is a recognised abbreviation for on

explanation.surface: A sect that dumped its leader last month, now a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal letters, this Latin term means of the previous month, so it stands for last month.

clue.text: Supports restricting clergyman's search

indicators.note: the supports restrict, or hold in, the clergyman's title

parts.note: feet are what support a body or piece of furniture
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: Supporters hemming in a clergyman's hunt for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret about is to rummage or search busily, from the animal used to hunt rabbits.

clue.text: Good gymnastic event elevated interest

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means raised up, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: the bar, as in parallel or high bar, is a gymnastic event

explanation.surface: A good gymnastics routine performed high up catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grabs you appeals to you, so the verb means to interest or attract.

clue.text: Pianist's sumptuous expression cut short

parts.note: rich means sumptuous or lavish

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A pianist's lavish phrasing is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sviatoslav Richter was a celebrated Soviet concert pianist, an example of a pianist.

clue.text: College employee backed removing front and reforming round building

indicators.note: backed means the shortened word reads back to front
the front letter of the word for a college teacher is removed

parts.note: a tutor is a teacher employed by a college

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college staff member, removed from the front, backs a reform of a circular building.
explanation.walkthrough: TUTOR loses its front T ('removing front') to give UTOR, 'backed' turns it to ROTU; 'reforming' makes NDA from AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, usually domed, an exact architectural term.

clue.text: Standard article eliminated by invader

indicators.note: the article is eliminated from the word for an invader

parts.note: a Norman was one of the 1066 invaders of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A standard item wiped out by an invading force.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a usual standard or expected level.

clue.text: Fashionable society confused by Adobe menu

indicators.note: the letters are confused, mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: High society left bewildered by a software menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means the fashionable world, the elite of society.

clue.text: Plant, special, planted in triangular area

indicators.note: the special letter is planted inside the word for the triangular area

parts.note: a gore is a triangular piece of cloth or land

explanation.surface: A special plant set in a triangular plot of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny yellow-flowered shrub, also called furze, is an example of a plant.
